newsitem.title: INDIA: Turkmenistan's Niyazov to sign pacts on India visit.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan's Niyazov to sign pacts on India visit.

text.p: India and Turkmenistan will sign four agreements, including one to avoid double taxation, during Turkmenistan President Saparmurat Niyazov's visit to New Delhi this week, Indian officials said on Monday.
Niyazov, who will arrive in India on a two-day state visit on Tuesday, is scheduled to meet President Shankar Dayal Sharma, Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and other senior officials.
"Essentially four documents will be signed during the visit," K. Raghunath, a senior Indian Foreign Ministry official, told a news conference.
Raghunath said the agreements were on avoidance of double taxation, cooperation in health and medicine, environment and forestry and the extension of cultural exchange programmes until 1999.
The two nations were also eager to jointly explore oil and natural gas fields in Turkmenistan, he said.
"We are willing to have third-country partnership in the field of hydrocarbons," Raghunath said.
The foreign ministers of India, Iran and Turkmenistan signed a transit agreement last week in Tehran for cargo traffic in the three countries and central Asian countries, he said.
"It is the latest step forward in the promotion of our trade with central Asian countries," said Raghunath.
